challenges.argument: As written this is the most cross-cutting Issue in the group, and it buys a safety net for a low-likelihood case: the round-2 second opinion rates it content/low (a select-all overwrite that is never undone in the session, or a deep link with overwrite=true). It touches Rust retention, the hot autosave path in writeTab, three deep-link writers, the daily append, the closed-note frontmatter rewrite and a help doc. writeTab is the same save path Issue 13 rewrites (closeTab saving through saveFileByPath), so the two will conflict. A naive pre-save snapshot also adds a save_snapshot IPC with a full-content SHA-256 to every 2 s autosave. Prepend and append keep the old text inside the new bytes, so their pre-write snapshot adds almost nothing.
challenges.evidence: Issue 08 lists writers at deep-link.service.ts:242-313, deep-link-actions.ts:55-71, frontmatter-write.service.ts:149-157, editor.service.ts:187-205 and history_repo.rs:82-89, and its gate is Both. editor.service.ts writeTab (HEAD, after saveFileByPath) is a bare writeTextFile + markSavedByPath + notifyAfterSave, run on every autosave. history.rs save_snapshot hashes the whole content on each call and dedupes only against the latest row. The Issue's own second opinion says 'Likelihood is low', and its Notes rank it 'last among the content items'.
challenges.alternative: For the first wave, keep the owner-decided retention change (history_repo.rs keeps the newest row per file, plus the help doc), the deep-link overwrite pre-write snapshot (the only destructive writer), and an editor baseline taken once per path per session (snapshot savedContent on the first in-app save, not on every save). Move the prepend, append, daily and closed-frontmatter writers to a later slot, and land the editor part after Issue 13 so it does not conflict in editor.service.ts.

challenges.argument: This is the only Issue in the group that needs Rust, Objective-C runtime work and a decision between patching tao and adding `applicationShouldTerminate:` to tao's delegate class at runtime. No automated test can cover it: every acceptance bullet is a manual Dock Quit, logout or shutdown check. A bug here risks stopping the app from quitting at logout or shutdown. The Issue's own note says that if the webview never answers, Quit does nothing, and NSTerminateLater would then hold up logout. The gain is small: at most the last 2 s after a typing pause, or 10 s in a continuous typing run, and only when the owner Dock-Quits or logs out within those seconds.

challenges.argument: This is the only content-safety Issue the plan ranks first, and it is still not in the wave. Cmd+D and Cmd+E are daily keys, and each one rewrites frontmatter above the caret. The caret then keeps its old numeric offset, so the next keystrokes go about 16 characters too early (or 1 too late after Cmd+E) and autosave writes that misplaced text to disk. The fix is size S: let CodeMirror map the selection instead of passing an unmapped cursor. First-wave Issue 131 edits the same replaceDoc try/catch and its shared spec() helper, so running 01 in the same wave avoids rework on those 30 lines.
challenges.evidence: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/MarkdownEditor.svelte:627 cursorPos = view.state.selection.main.head is read from the old doc. :182-186 spec() dispatches changes together with selection: EditorSelection.cursor(Math.min(cursorPos, text.length)), and CodeMirror takes an explicit selection as already post-change. :219-222 showTabState repeats this on a revisit. The trigger is frontmatter-write.service.ts:131 syncExternalContentToEditor, reached from Cmd+D/Cmd+E (global-keybindings.ts:191-202). First-wave 131-note-whose-live-preview-widget-throws-every.md:5,22 changes replaceDoc's catch/rebuild path (:187-197), which reuses spec(). No test asserts the caret after a sync.
challenges.alternative: Run it right before 131 so 131 rebases onto the mapped spec(). If the wave needs a smaller cut, at least make the replaceDoc change (:182-186) and leave the showTabState revisit for later.

Part F101 (a language switch deletes title="..." or {1,3}) changes buildLanguageSelect and code-block-widget.test.ts, the same lines and test file that first-wave 73 changes through COMMON_LANGUAGES. challenges.argument: Kanban is daily, and renaming a lane silently turns off its card limit, auto-complete-on-drop and collapsed state. The stale key also stays in the settings block, so a later lane with the old title inherits those settings. The fix is a few lines in one pure function with a logic test. First-wave 123 changes renameLane in the same function and the same kanban.logic.test.ts, so doing them together costs almost nothing, while waiting means reopening the same function after 123 merges.

Every getter keys on title: :595 collapsed, :616 maxItems, :647 autoComplete (laneSettings?.[laneTitle]). kanban.types.ts:55 laneSettings is a Record<string, ...> keyed by title. 123-kanban-lane-actions-never-turn-raw-into.md:5,22,27 lists renameLane among the functions it changes and tests.
challenges.alternative: Run it right after 123 (or let 123's agent take its single criterion), since both edit renameLane and kanban.logic.test.ts.

challenges.argument: Views are in the owner's daily list, and the Filter panel's own number operators produce `prop < value`. Every note that lacks the property then counts as 0 and passes `priority < 3` or `estimated_hours <= 2`, so a daily view lists the wrong notes. The fix is a null guard in one pure function, with an evaluator test and an executeQuery test. It conflicts with nothing: first-wave 51 touches validateExpression in the same file, about 400 lines away.
challenges.evidence: src/lib/features/collection/expression/evaluator.ts:708-715 compareValues guards only Dates and then returns toNumber(a) - toNumber(b). :624-629 toNumber(null) is 0, and :620 resolves a missing property to null. The date branch already treats null as NaN (dateOperandTime). The Filter panel emits `prop < value` for numbers (filter.logic.ts:63-70, per the Issue). 51-formula-that-calls-unknown-function-cannot-confirmed.md changes validateExpression at evaluator.ts:306-316.
challenges.alternative: No partial fix needed: it is already S. It can run at any point in the wave.

challenges.argument: The owner's first wave already spends Issues 08 and 102 on File History being trustworthy, and the help tells users to recover moved notes through it. Today every daily rename or move hides a note's history, and a new note at the old path shows the old note's versions, so a restore from that list would bring back the wrong note's text. Five first-wave Issues (21, 31, 112, 124, 126) restructure applyPathChange, where this Issue's new leg goes. Adding it while that code is being reworked, next to rename_note, is cheaper than reopening it afterwards. The cost is higher than the others (Rust command, IPC contract, both gates), so it ranks last.
challenges.evidence: rg finds no rename_history and no UPDATE snapshots in src-tauri/src or src/lib. src/lib/core/filesystem/path-change.service.ts:209-211 calls rename_note but has no history leg. Snapshot keys are vault-relative paths (file-history.service.ts:27, :115, per the Issue). help/documentation/22-auto-move.md:177,188 points users to File History for moved files. applyPathChange is cited by first-wave 21, 31, 112, 124 and 126.
challenges.alternative: If the Rust and IPC cost is too much for this wave, schedule it right after 126, the last first-wave Issue that reshapes applyPathChange. Keep the Trash-restore re-key criterion for later.

agreed: The other 24 should wait, and these were checked against HEAD where the call depended on it. 18 is not a daily trigger: the app's own image writes use ![[...]] (deep-link-actions.ts:110) or file:// (deep-link.logic.ts:274), and 18 is blocked by 10 anyway. 11 is an M renderer change with only display impact, and the owner chose to leave it out after recording a decision on it. 19, 42 and 53 are uncommon display issues. 37, 39, 46, 47, 49, 50, 57, 58 and 59 are occasional, low or non-daily flows: theme editing, updates, a rarely toggled setting, the graph view, semantic mode, path-style create, very large vocabularies. 30, 38, 54, 61, 63, 65 and 72 are polish or narrow UX. 74, 76 and 78 are docs-only. None of them puts written content at risk or collides with a first-wave change.

challenges.argument: First-wave Issue 98 rewrites writeTab so it reads the disk before every tab write. That new read rejects with not-found when a note was deleted or renamed outside the app, and 98 has no criterion for that case, so its agent will have to invent a behavior. Issue 99 decides it: create:false, close a clean tab, mark a dirty tab orphaned. If 99 waits, writeTab, reloadExternallyChangedTabs and the same editor.service.test.ts describes get rewritten twice by two agents, which is a sure merge conflict and design drift. The trigger is also the owner's own stated workflow: an agent or git editing files outside the app. A delete or rename of an open note comes back on the next keystroke or calendar drag, so an intended delete is undone and post-rename typing lands in a ghost file.
challenges.evidence: src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:186-204 writeTab calls writeTextFile(path, content) with no options (plugin-fs defaults to create:true); :438-441 a rejected reload read only logs at debug and keeps the tab; 98 acceptance criteria (98-...md:47-52) add the pre-write disk read and change the 'editor always wins' test with no not-found case; 137-...md Notes: the owner expects 'an agent editing files outside the app'.
challenges.alternative: Pair with 98 in the same worktree, or schedule it right after 98 with Blocked by: 98 so it builds on 98's pre-write read instead of colliding with it.

challenges.argument: Most of 121 is millisecond races and should wait. Its no-op-commit section is different: it needs no timing, it deletes text the user typed, and the fix is one guard. A Properties-panel commit that leaves the content unchanged still arms skipNextParseFor. The next editor edit to the frontmatter then skips its only re-parse, and the next panel edit rebuilds the block from the stale store and deletes the typed line, which then autosaves. Properties and meta-bind are daily flows, and undo cannot restore the line (addToHistory false).
challenges.evidence: src/lib/features/properties/properties.service.ts:96-99 builds newContent and sets skipNextParseFor = activePath with no newContent === content check; :37-41 consumeSkipNextParse skips whatever the content is; PropertyField.svelte:72-77 a number field commits Number(input.value), so '5.' or '5.0' over 5 is a no-op commit; 121-...md:156-163 has the trigger and two criteria for this section.
challenges.alternative: Split the no-op-commit section into its own S Issue (return before arming the flag when newContent === content, plus its two criteria) and leave the rest of 121 in the later wave.

challenges.argument: The owner uses canvas daily, and this is the one canvas defect that destroys written content. A typo left in the app's own canvas source mode is enough: switching tabs resets source mode, and the board then renders empty with '+ Add card'. The first click serializes {nodes:[new]} over the whole file. File History softens it only when an earlier valid in-app save exists within retention. First-wave 06 and 52 both rework persistWithoutHistory and the sync effect in CanvasInner.svelte, the same code 101 must guard. Landing it in the same wave avoids a third rebase over that code.
challenges.evidence: src/lib/features/canvas/canvas.logic.ts:36-49 parseCanvas returns createEmptyCanvas() on any parse or shape failure; src/lib/app/EditorView.svelte:46-51 resets canvasSourceMode on a tab switch; CanvasInner.svelte:591 '+ Add card'; 06-...md:5,52 and 52-...md:23 both edit CanvasInner persistWithoutHistory (:118-123).
challenges.alternative: Schedule it right after 06 (Blocked by: 06) so it adds the parse guard to 06's path-keyed persist instead of the current one.

challenges.argument: Agents now write the owner's notes, and an unquoted `up: [[Home]]` or `- [[Carol]]` is exactly what agents and hand edits produce. On such a note, every meta-bind toggle, Properties edit, Cmd+D/Cmd+E, icon set and archive is refused with a 'nested values' toast, though the rewrite would lose nothing. That hits meta-bind, a daily flow, on every such note. The fix is S, frontend only, pure logic in one function, and the owner decision is already recorded.

challenges.argument: Views are a daily flow. On any calendar-type view, the 4th and later notes of a busy day (meetings, or a calendar over file.mtime) cannot be opened from the calendar at all: '+N more' is a bare span and the day number is not a control. The fix is S and self-contained in one component with a new test file. It collides with no first-wave Issue and carries no data risk.

agreed: The rest look right where they are. Most are millisecond-window races (105, 121's other sections, 125), opt-in Auto Move or rare-file paths (109, 111, 119, 120), refactors or deferred Rust work (137, 148-150), polish on surfaces that are not daily (91, 92, 144), or Issues blocked by first-wave work (89 on 71, 146 on 145, 138 on 137). For 130, the no-vault trigger is gone: dispatch_shortcut returns early unless db::is_open() (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:45-47). Its windowless trigger is fixed by first-wave 04. 109's canvas section is covered by first-wave 15, and 97's JSON sections by 116. 107 and 100 are large changes (a Rust writer for every note writer, and an IPC DTO change) for disk-full or dropped-FSEvents triggers.
